title: The Dairy Farm: Multiplication
seo_title: Multiplication Class 5 Worksheet with Answers (Maths Mela Chapter 6)
standard_code: Class 5, Maths Mela Chapter 6: The Dairy Farm
standard_text: Multiplication of larger numbers: mental strategies, multiplying by 10, 100 and 1,000, the standard method for 2- and 3-digit numbers, and problems (summary of NCERT Maths Mela Class 5)
meta_desc: Class 5 The Dairy Farm worksheet (Maths Mela Chapter 6): mental methods, area models, short and long multiplication and stories. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Split numbers to multiply in parts.
key_sub: Multiply by tens, then ones, and add.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • 24 × 35 = 24 × 30 + 24 × 5 = 720 + 120 = 840.
  • Long multiplication: multiply by the ones, then the tens (add a 0), then add.

Examples

Example

A farm gets 245 litres of milk a day. How much in 12 days?

245 × 10 = 2,450

245 × 2 = 490

2,450 + 490

Answer: 2,940 litres

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Forgetting the 0 when multiplying by tensThe tens row starts with a 0.
Adding the partial products wronglyLine up the rows before adding.

faq.a: A written method for multiplying by a 2-digit number using two rows of partial products.

items.e: 24 is double 12, so 24 × 7 is double 84 = 168.

items.q: What is 19 × 6? (Hint: 19 is 1 less than 20.)
What is 16 × 25? (Hint: halve one number and double the other.)
items.e: Halve 16 and double 25: 16 × 25 = 8 × 50 = 4 × 100 = 400. If you double one number you must halve the other.

items.q: What is 60 × 7?
items.e: 60 is 6 tens. 6 × 7 = 42, so 6 tens × 7 = 42 tens = 420.

items.q: What is 25 × 4 × 9?
items.e: You can multiply in any order. 25 × 4 = 100, then 100 × 9 = 900. Multiply all three numbers, not just two.

items.q: Multiply by 10, then halve, to find 46 × 5.
items.e: × 5 is the same as × 10, then halve. 46 × 10 = 460. Half of 460 = 230.

items.q: What is 30 × 400?
items.e: Use 3 × 4 = 12, then put back all 3 zeros (one in 30, two in 400): 30 × 400 = 12,000.

items.q: What is 900 × 8?
items.e: 900 is 9 hundreds. 9 × 8 = 72, so 9 hundreds × 8 = 72 hundreds = 7,200.

items.q: What is 4 × 19 × 25?
items.e: You can multiply in any order. Change the order: 4 × 25 = 100, then 100 × 19 = 1,900. Multiply all three numbers, not just two.

items.q: What is 400 × 6?
items.e: 400 is 4 hundreds. 4 × 6 = 24, so 4 hundreds × 6 = 24 hundreds = 2,400.

items.q: What is 27 × 1,000?
items.e: × 1,000 moves every digit three places to the left: 27 × 1,000 = 27 000 (three zeros on the end).

items.q: Double, then double again, to find 37 × 4.
items.e: × 4 is double, then double again. Double 37 = 74. Double 74 = 148. Doubling only once gives 74; three times gives 296.

items.q: What is 2 × 36 × 5?
items.e: You can multiply in any order. Change the order: 2 × 5 = 10, then 10 × 36 = 360. Multiply all three numbers, not just two.

items.q: What is 25 × 4 × 7?
items.e: You can multiply in any order. 25 × 4 = 100, then 100 × 7 = 700. Multiply all three numbers, not just two.

items.q: What is 18 × 50?
items.e: × 50 is the same as × 100, then halve. 18 × 100 = 1,800. Half of 1,800 = 900.

items.q: What is 5 × 17 × 2?
items.e: You can multiply in any order. Change the order: 5 × 2 = 10, then 10 × 17 = 170. Multiply all three numbers, not just two.

items.q: What is 99 × 6? (Hint: 99 is 1 less than 100.)

items.e: 24 is one less than 25, so take away one 8: 200 − 8 = 192.

items.q: What is 58 × 100?
items.e: × 100 makes every digit 100 times bigger: the 8 ones become 8 hundreds. 58 × 100 = 5,800 (two zeros on the end).

items.q: What is 70 × 80?
items.e: Use 7 × 8 = 56. 70 has one zero and 80 has one zero, so put back two zeros: 70 × 80 = 5,600.

items.q: Which parts add up to 74 × 65?
items.e: Each part of one number multiplies each part of the other, so there are 4 parts. Partition 74 = 70 + 4 and 65 = 60 + 5. 70 × 60 = 4,200, 4 × 60 = 240, 70 × 5 = 350, 4 × 5 = 20. Add: 4,200 + 240 + 350 + 20 = 4,810.

items.q: Which is equal to 48 × 7?
items.e: Partition 48 into 40 + 8. Both parts must be multiplied by 7: 40 × 7 + 8 × 7 = 280 + 56 = 336.

items.q: What number goes in the part marked ?
items.e: The ? part is 5 wide and 9 tall: 5 × 9 = 45. All four parts add to 75 × 49 = 3,675.

items.q: What number goes in the part marked ?
items.e: The ? part is 50 wide and 5 tall: 50 × 5 = 250. All four parts add to 53 × 65 = 3,445.

items.q: Which parts add up to 57 × 24?
items.e: Each part of one number multiplies each part of the other, so there are 4 parts. Partition 57 = 50 + 7 and 24 = 20 + 4. 50 × 20 = 1,000, 7 × 20 = 140, 50 × 4 = 200, 7 × 4 = 28. Add: 1,000 + 140 + 200 + 28 = 1,368.

items.q: What number goes in the part marked ?
items.e: The ? part is 30 wide and 50 tall: 30 × 50 = 1,500. Think: 3 tens × 5 tens = 15 hundreds. All four parts add to 37 × 57 = 2,109.

Use the area model to find 34 × 5.
Use the area model to find 75 × 24.
Which is equal to 74 × 5?
items.e: Partition 74 into 70 + 4. Both parts must be multiplied by 5: 70 × 5 + 4 × 5 = 350 + 20 = 370.

items.e: The ? part is 9 wide and 20 tall: 9 × 20 = 180. All four parts add to 69 × 25 = 1,725.

items.q: Use the area model to find 526 × 9.
Which parts add up to 47 × 32?
items.e: Each part of one number multiplies each part of the other, so there are 4 parts. Partition 47 = 40 + 7 and 32 = 30 + 2. 40 × 30 = 1,200, 7 × 30 = 210, 40 × 2 = 80, 7 × 2 = 14. Add: 1,200 + 210 + 80 + 14 = 1,504.

items.q: Use the area model to find 119 × 9.
Which is equal to 49 × 6?
items.e: Partition 49 into 40 + 9. Both parts must be multiplied by 6: 40 × 6 + 9 × 6 = 240 + 54 = 294.

items.q: Calculate 9,462 × 7
items.e: Ones: 2 × 7 = 14. Write 4, exchange 1. Tens: 6 × 7 + 1 = 43. Write 3, exchange 4. Hundreds: 4 × 7 + 4 = 32. Write 2, exchange 3. Thousands: 9 × 7 + 3 = 66. Write 66. Answer: 66,234.

items.q: Use short multiplication.
items.e: Ones: 6 × 7 = 42. Write 2, exchange 4. Tens: 6 × 7 + 4 = 46. Write 6, exchange 4. Hundreds: 3 × 7 + 4 = 25. Write 5, exchange 2. Thousands: 4 × 7 + 2 = 30. Write 30. Answer: 30,562.

items.q: Use short multiplication.
items.e: Ones: 3 × 9 = 27. Write 7, exchange 2. Tens: 1 × 9 + 2 = 11. Write 1, exchange 1. Hundreds: 1 × 9 + 1 = 10. Write 0, exchange 1. Thousands: 7 × 9 + 1 = 64. Write 64. Answer: 64,017.

items.q: Calculate 339 × 3
items.e: Ones: 9 × 3 = 27. Write 7, exchange 2. Tens: 3 × 3 + 2 = 11. Write 1, exchange 1. Hundreds: 3 × 3 + 1 = 10. Write 10. Answer: 1,017.

items.q: Calculate 539 × 4
items.e: Ones: 9 × 4 = 36. Write 6, exchange 3. Tens: 3 × 4 + 3 = 15. Write 5, exchange 1. Hundreds: 5 × 4 + 1 = 21. Write 21. Answer: 2,156.

items.q: Calculate 5,495 × 3
items.e: Ones: 5 × 3 = 15. Write 5, exchange 1. Tens: 9 × 3 + 1 = 28. Write 8, exchange 2. Hundreds: 4 × 3 + 2 = 14. Write 4, exchange 1. Thousands: 5 × 3 + 1 = 16. Write 16. Answer: 16,485.

items.q: Calculate 9,087 × 8
items.e: Ones: 7 × 8 = 56. Write 6, exchange 5. Tens: 8 × 8 + 5 = 69. Write 9, exchange 6. Hundreds: 0 × 8 + 6 = 6. Write 6. Thousands: 9 × 8 = 72. Write 72. Answer: 72,696. 0 × 8 = 0, but you still add the exchanged 6.

items.q: Use short multiplication.
items.e: Ones: 8 × 4 = 32. Write 2, exchange 3. Tens: 0 × 4 + 3 = 3. Write 3. Hundreds: 8 × 4 = 32. Write 2, exchange 3. Thousands: 9 × 4 + 3 = 39. Write 39. Answer: 39,232. 0 × 4 = 0, but you still add the exchanged 3.

items.e: Thousands column: 5 × 7 = 35, then add the exchanged 6: 41. Write 41. The ? is the thousands digit, 1. Full working: Ones: 7 × 7 = 49. Write 9, exchange 4. Tens: 5 × 7 + 4 = 39. Write 9, exchange 3. Hundreds: 9 × 7 + 3 = 66. Write 6, exchange 6. Thousands: 5 × 7 + 6 = 41. Write 41. Answer: 41,699.

items.q: Calculate 5,728 × 9
items.e: Ones: 8 × 9 = 72. Write 2, exchange 7. Tens: 2 × 9 + 7 = 25. Write 5, exchange 2. Hundreds: 7 × 9 + 2 = 65. Write 5, exchange 6. Thousands: 5 × 9 + 6 = 51. Write 51. Answer: 51,552.

items.q: Use short multiplication.
items.e: Ones: 3 × 6 = 18. Write 8, regroup 1. Tens: 7 × 6 + 1 = 43. Write 3, regroup 4. Hundreds: 6 × 6 + 4 = 40. Write 40. Answer: 4,038.

items.q: Use short multiplication.
items.e: Ones: 6 × 4 = 24. Write 4, regroup 2. Tens: 8 × 4 + 2 = 34. Write 4, regroup 3. Hundreds: 6 × 4 + 3 = 27. Write 7, regroup 2. Thousands: 2 × 4 + 2 = 10. Write 10. Answer: 10,744.

items.q: Calculate 257 × 8.
items.e: Ones: 7 × 8 = 56. Write 6, regroup 5. Tens: 5 × 8 + 5 = 45. Write 5, regroup 4. Hundreds: 2 × 8 + 4 = 20. Write 20. Answer: 2,056.

items.q: What digit goes in the box marked ?
items.e: Tens column: 2 × 9 = 18, then add the regrouped 1: 19. Write 9, regroup 1. Full working: Ones: 2 × 9 = 18. Write 8, regroup 1. Tens: 2 × 9 + 1 = 19. Write 9, regroup 1. Hundreds: 6 × 9 + 1 = 55. Write 5, regroup 5. Thousands: 3 × 9 + 5 = 32. Write 32. Answer: 32,598.

items.q: Use short multiplication.
items.e: Ones: 4 × 6 = 24. Write 4, regroup 2. Tens: 8 × 6 + 2 = 50. Write 0, regroup 5. Hundreds: 8 × 6 + 5 = 53. Write 3, regroup 5. Thousands: 7 × 6 + 5 = 47. Write 47. Answer: 47,304.

items.q: Calculate 4,072 × 8.
items.e: Ones: 2 × 8 = 16. Write 6, regroup 1. Tens: 7 × 8 + 1 = 57. Write 7, regroup 5. Hundreds: 0 × 8 + 5 = 5. Write 5. Thousands: 4 × 8 = 32. Write 32. Answer: 32,576. 0 × 8 = 0, but you still add the regrouped 5.

items.q: What digit goes in the box marked ?
items.e: Hundreds column: 9 × 8 = 72, then add the regrouped 4: 76. Write 6, regroup 7. Full working: Ones: 6 × 8 = 48. Write 8, regroup 4. Tens: 5 × 8 + 4 = 44. Write 4, regroup 4. Hundreds: 9 × 8 + 4 = 76. Write 6, regroup 7. Thousands: 5 × 8 + 7 = 47. Write 47. Answer: 47,648.

items.q: Calculate 965 × 3.
items.e: Ones: 5 × 3 = 15. Write 5, regroup 1. Tens: 6 × 3 + 1 = 19. Write 9, regroup 1. Hundreds: 9 × 3 + 1 = 28. Write 28. Answer: 2,895.

items.q: What digit goes in the box marked ?
items.e: Hundreds column: 7 × 3 = 21, then add the regrouped 2: 23. Write 3, regroup 2. Full working: Ones: 9 × 3 = 27. Write 7, regroup 2. Tens: 9 × 3 + 2 = 29. Write 9, regroup 2. Hundreds: 7 × 3 + 2 = 23. Write 3, regroup 2. Thousands: 6 × 3 + 2 = 20. Write 20. Answer: 20,397.

items.q: Calculate 9,739 × 6.
items.e: Ones: 9 × 6 = 54. Write 4, regroup 5. Tens: 3 × 6 + 5 = 23. Write 3, regroup 2. Hundreds: 7 × 6 + 2 = 44. Write 4, regroup 4. Thousands: 9 × 6 + 4 = 58. Write 58. Answer: 58,434.

items.q: Om got 44 × 78 = 3,402. What mistake did he make?
c: Did not add an exchanged digit
items.e: Row 1 should be 352, not 322: 4 × 8 = 32, write 2, exchange 3; 4 × 8 + 3 = 35, write 35. The exchanged digits were not added. The correct answer is 3,432.

items.q: Use long multiplication.
Use long multiplication.
What number goes in the dashed box?
items.e: Row 1 is 66 × 3: 6 × 3 = 18, write 8, exchange 1; 6 × 3 + 1 = 19, write 19. So the row is 198. Check: 198 + 1,320 = 1,518.

items.q: Use long multiplication.
Use long multiplication.
What number goes in the dashed box?
items.e: Row 2 multiplies by the tens digit, so it is 85 × 70. Write the place-holder 0 first, then 85 × 7: 5 × 7 = 35, write 5, exchange 3; 8 × 7 + 3 = 59, write 59. The row is 5,950, not 595. Check: 680 + 5,950 = 6,630.

items.q: Aarav got 49 × 76 = 637. What mistake did he make?
c: Did not add an exchanged digit
items.e: Row 2 should be 49 × 70 = 3,430, but he wrote 343. The place-holder 0 is missing. The correct answer is 3,724.

items.q: What number goes in the dashed box?
items.e: Row 2 multiplies by the tens digit, so it is 77 × 60. Write the place-holder 0 first, then 77 × 6: 7 × 6 = 42, write 2, exchange 4; 7 × 6 + 4 = 46, write 46. The row is 4,620, not 462. Check: 308 + 4,620 = 4,928.

items.q: What number goes in the dashed box?
items.e: Row 1 is 74 × 4: 4 × 4 = 16, write 6, exchange 1; 7 × 4 + 1 = 29, write 29. So the row is 296. Check: 296 + 6,660 = 6,956.

c: Did not add a regrouped digit
items.e: Row 1 should be 45, not 35: 5 × 3 = 15, write 5, regroup 1; 1 × 3 + 1 = 4, write 4. The regrouped digits were not added. The correct answer is 795.

items.q: Rehan got 13 × 59 = 182. What mistake did he make?
c: Did not add a regrouped digit
items.e: Row 2 should be 13 × 50 = 650, but he wrote 65. The place-holder 0 is missing. The correct answer is 767.

items.q: What number goes in the dashed box?
items.e: Row 2 multiplies by the tens digit, so it is 855 × 60. Write the place-holder 0 first, then 855 × 6: 5 × 6 = 30, write 0, regroup 3; 5 × 6 + 3 = 33, write 3, regroup 3; 8 × 6 + 3 = 51, write 51. The row is 51,300, not 5,130. Check: 5,985 + 51,300 = 57,285.

items.q: What number goes in the dashed box?
items.e: Row 2 multiplies by the tens digit, so it is 32 × 90. Write the place-holder 0 first, then 32 × 9: 2 × 9 = 18, write 8, regroup 1; 3 × 9 + 1 = 28, write 28. The row is 2,880, not 288. Check: 224 + 2,880 = 3,104.

items.q: Calculate 349 × 74.
What number goes in the dashed box?
items.e: Add the two rows with column addition, and add every regrouped digit: 2,871 + 9,570 = 12,441.

items.q: Use long multiplication.
A school books 6 coaches with 49 seats each. 250 students and 22 adults go on the trip. How many seats are empty?
items.e: Step 1: seats: 6 × 49 = 294 (9 × 6 = 54, write 4, exchange 5; 4 × 6 + 5 = 29). Step 2: people: 250 + 22 = 272. Step 3: empty seats: 294 − 272 = 22.

items.q: A recipe for 4 people uses 175 g of flour. How much flour is needed for 12 people?
items.e: 12 people is 3 times as many as 4 people (4 × 3 = 12), so use 3 times as much flour: 175 × 3 = 525 g. Do not multiply by 12: the recipe is for 4 people, not 1.

items.q: A family uses 165 litres of water a day. How much water do they use in a week?
items.e: Equal groups: 7 days × 165 litres, so multiply 165 × 7. Ones: 5 × 7 = 35. Write 5, exchange 3. Tens: 6 × 7 + 3 = 45. Write 5, exchange 4. Hundreds: 1 × 7 + 4 = 11. Write 11. Answer: 1,155.

items.q: A gardener is paid ₹12 an hour. She works for 15 hours this week. How much does she earn?
items.e: Equal groups: 15 hours × ₹12, so multiply 12 × 15. Row 1: 12 × 5 = 60. Row 2: 12 × 10 = 120 (write the place-holder 0, then 12 × 1 = 12). Add: 60 + 120 = 180.

items.q: A dripping tap wastes 45 mL of water every hour. How much water does it waste in 24 hours?
items.e: Equal groups: 24 hours × 45 mL, so multiply 45 × 24. Row 1: 45 × 4 = 180. Row 2: 45 × 20 = 900 (write the place-holder 0, then 45 × 2 = 90). Add: 180 + 900 = 1,080.

items.q: A box holds 144 pencils. The school office orders 23 boxes. How many pencils is that?
items.e: Equal groups: 23 boxes × 144 pencils, so multiply 144 × 23. Row 1: 144 × 3 = 432. Row 2: 144 × 20 = 2,880 (write the place-holder 0, then 144 × 2 = 288). Add: 432 + 2,880 = 3,312.

items.q: A train travels 125 km every hour. How far does it travel in 3 hours?
items.e: Equal groups: 3 hours × 125 km, so multiply 125 × 3. Ones: 5 × 3 = 15. Write 5, exchange 1. Tens: 2 × 3 + 1 = 7. Write 7. Hundreds: 1 × 3 = 3. Write 3. Answer: 375.

items.q: Rohan cycles 18 km every day for 14 days. How far does he cycle altogether?
items.e: Equal groups: 14 days × 18 km, so multiply 18 × 14. Row 1: 18 × 4 = 72. Row 2: 18 × 10 = 180 (write the place-holder 0, then 18 × 1 = 18). Add: 72 + 180 = 252.

items.q: A crate holds 24 bottles of milk. The school orders 35 crates this term. How many bottles is that?
items.e: Equal groups: 35 crates × 24 bottles, so multiply 24 × 35. Row 1: 24 × 5 = 120. Row 2: 24 × 30 = 720 (write the place-holder 0, then 24 × 3 = 72). Add: 120 + 720 = 840.

items.q: A lorry carries 32 crates. Each crate has a mass of 145 kg. What is the total mass of the crates?
items.e: Equal groups: 32 crates × 145 kg, so multiply 145 × 32. Row 1: 145 × 2 = 290. Row 2: 145 × 30 = 4,350 (write the place-holder 0, then 145 × 3 = 435). Add: 290 + 4,350 = 4,640.

items.q: At swimming training, Karan swims 36 laps of a 50 m pool. How far does he swim?
items.e: Equal groups: 36 laps × 50 m, so multiply 50 × 36. Row 1: 50 × 6 = 300. Row 2: 50 × 30 = 1,500 (write the place-holder 0, then 50 × 3 = 150). Add: 300 + 1,500 = 1,800.

items.q: A mango farm in Queensland packs 1,235 trays in a week. Each tray holds 18 mangoes. How many mangoes is that?
items.e: Equal groups: 1,235 trays × 18 mangoes, so multiply 1,235 × 18. Row 1: 1,235 × 8 = 9,880. Row 2: 1,235 × 10 = 12,350 (write the place-holder 0, then 1,235 × 1 = 1,235). Add: 9,880 + 12,350 = 22,230.

items.q: The school library orders 165 new books at ₹14 each. What is the total cost?
items.e: Equal groups: 165 books × ₹14, so multiply 165 × 14. Row 1: 165 × 4 = 660. Row 2: 165 × 10 = 1,650 (write the place-holder 0, then 165 × 1 = 165). Add: 660 + 1,650 = 2,310.

items.q: A delivery truck drives 386 km every week. How far does it drive in 7 weeks?
items.e: Equal groups: 7 weeks × 386 km, so multiply 386 × 7. Ones: 6 × 7 = 42. Write 2, regroup 4. Tens: 8 × 7 + 4 = 60. Write 0, regroup 6. Hundreds: 3 × 7 + 6 = 27. Write 27. Answer: 2,702.

items.q: A school excursion to the zoo costs ₹35 for each student. 28 students in Class 5 are going. What is the total cost?
items.e: Equal groups: 28 students × ₹35, so multiply 35 × 28. Row 1: 35 × 8 = 280. Row 2: 35 × 20 = 700 (write the place-holder 0, then 35 × 2 = 70). Add: 280 + 700 = 980.

items.q: The school canteen sells 136 meat pies each week. How many pies does it sell in 9 weeks?
items.e: Equal groups: 9 weeks × 136 pies, so multiply 136 × 9. Ones: 6 × 9 = 54. Write 4, regroup 5. Tens: 3 × 9 + 5 = 32. Write 2, regroup 3. Hundreds: 1 × 9 + 3 = 12. Write 12. Answer: 1,224.

items.q: The school hall is set up with 32 rows of chairs. Each row has 26 chairs. How many chairs are there?
items.e: Equal groups: 32 rows × 26 chairs, so multiply 26 × 32. Row 1: 26 × 2 = 52. Row 2: 26 × 30 = 780 (write the place-holder 0, then 26 × 3 = 78). Add: 52 + 780 = 832.

items.q: A bakery makes 1,365 sausage rolls every day. How many sausage rolls does it make in 6 days?
items.e: Equal groups: 6 days × 1,365 sausage rolls, so multiply 1,365 × 6. Ones: 5 × 6 = 30. Write 0, regroup 3. Tens: 6 × 6 + 3 = 39. Write 9, regroup 3. Hundreds: 3 × 6 + 3 = 21. Write 1, regroup 2. Thousands: 1 × 6 + 2 = 8. Write 8. Answer: 8,190.

items.q: A stand at the cricket ground has 24 rows of 45 seats. 958 people are sitting in the stand. How many seats are empty?
For the athletics carnival, the school orders 35 boxes of water bottles. Each box holds 24 bottles. How many bottles is that?
items.e: Equal groups: 35 boxes × 24 bottles, so multiply 24 × 35. Row 1: 24 × 5 = 120. Row 2: 24 × 30 = 720 (write the place-holder 0, then 24 × 3 = 72). Add: 120 + 720 = 840.
